records.title: The effects of a higher protein intake during energy restriction on changes in body composition and physical function in older women.

first_pass_scientific_annotation.design_material: Double-blind randomized trial of 31 overweight or obese postmenopausal women: a prescribed 1,400 kcal/day diet plus 2 × 25 g/day whey protein (15) versus maltodextrin (16) for 6 months. The assigned supplement contrast is explicit; diet/macronutrient prescription is shared.
first_pass_scientific_annotation.measured_function_or_other: Isokinetic knee strength, balance and a physical performance battery, alongside DXA and MRI composition. Up-and-go and transfer tests appear in composition–performance regression analyses.
first_pass_scientific_annotation.results_limits: Strength, balance and physical performance changes did not differ between groups (all p > .05). Weight loss difference was p = .059; composition effects and regressions predicting improved tasks are not a demonstrated between-arm functional benefit. PRO lost 4.2% more absolute muscle (p = .01) while relative muscle favored PRO. The conclusion that protein enhances function is broader than the reported functional contrast.

first_pass_scientific_annotation.design_material: Version-1 preprint pooled intention-to-treat analysis of two randomized Japanese community trials (N = 155), all given a shared 6-month multimodal exercise/self-monitoring program. Assigned add-ons were balanced ONS, protein-fortified beverage, nutrition counseling or control; exact formulations/doses absent.
first_pass_scientific_annotation.measured_function_or_other: Primary early undernutrition risk score; secondary measured handgrip strength plus weight/BMI/FFMI, MNA-SF and depression. Grip measurement method not described.

records.title: Caffeine supplementation improved movement patterns and reactive agility in rugby sevens matches in male collegiate players.

records.title: Oxidative stress, inflammation and recovery of muscle function after damaging exercise: effect of 6-week mixed antioxidant supplementation.

first_pass_scientific_annotation.design_material: Thirty-eight men randomized double-blind to placebo (18) or mixed antioxidants primarily C/E (20) for 6 weeks, then 90 minutes intermittent shuttle running. Exact doses, ingredients and placebo contents absent.
first_pass_scientific_annotation.measured_function_or_other: Actual isometric knee flexor/extensor torque and ROM tracked before/after exercise up to 168 hours; oxidative, cortisol and IL-6 measures.
first_pass_scientific_annotation.results_limits: Torque fell 9–19% and remained reduced during first 48 hours, without between-arm difference. Supplementation neither facilitated muscle-function recovery nor reduced oxidative/inflammatory markers. Isoprostane response differed (P = .04) with a tendency higher in supplemented patients; IL-6 was higher at 1 hour (11.3 ± 3.4 versus 6.2 ± 3.8 pg/mL, P = .05), while cortisol rise was attenuated.

first_pass_scientific_annotation.measured_function_or_other: Objective peak torque, oxygen kinetics and subjective perceived exertion during cycling; lactate.
first_pass_scientific_annotation.results_limits: Peak torque null (placebo 144.6 ± 18.6 versus caffeine 143.9 ± 18.7 N·m), as were oxygen time constant/slow component. records.title: Grapefruit juice-simvastatin interaction: effect on serum concentrations of simvastatin, simvastatin acid, and HMG-CoA reductase inhibitors.

first_pass_scientific_annotation.design_material: Randomized two-period crossover in 10 healthy volunteers: double-strength grapefruit juice 200 mL or water three times daily for 2 days; on day 3 oral simvastatin 60 mg with juice/water plus two further 200 mL portions at 0.5 and 1.5 hours. Exact juice composition and washout absent.
first_pass_scientific_annotation.measured_function_or_other: Serum simvastatin/acid pharmacokinetics and active/total HMG-CoA reductase inhibitory activity. No physical function or clinical lipid outcome.
first_pass_scientific_annotation.results_limits: Juice increased simvastatin mean Cmax about 9-fold and AUC 16-fold, acid measures about 7-fold, and active/total inhibitory AUC 2.4/3.6-fold. These exposure increases and proposed CYP3A4 inhibition are an interaction warning, not efficacy or functional benefit.

first_pass_scientific_annotation.measured_function_or_other: FACIT-Fatigue subjective illness-related fatigue is secondary, score 0–52 with higher less fatigue; no objective physical task. MMRM contrasts and mediation adjustment for ACR20 (prespecified) versus MDA/CRP (post hoc).
first_pass_scientific_annotation.results_limits: Week-24 fatigue improvements 5.6–7.6 versus placebo 2.2–3.6 and ≥4-point responses 54–63% versus 35–46%. Two-trial secondary analysis is not a newly read independent trial.

records.title: Does Sport-Drink Use During Exercise Promote an Acute Positive Energy Balance?

first_pass_scientific_annotation.context_subrole: derived literature analysis of energy balance
first_pass_scientific_annotation.design_material: Uses 11 existing sports-drink versus placebo exercise studies and calculates energy intake/expenditure; no new administered participant cohort.
first_pass_scientific_annotation.measured_function_or_other: Derived caloric balance from VO2/RER/duration and carbohydrate dosing; original studies focused on physical performance, but their source results are not presented here.
first_pass_scientific_annotation.results_limits: Mean energy deficit remained despite sports-drink use during ≥60-minute exercise. first_pass_scientific_annotation.measured_function_or_other: Actual race performance time, subjective gut comfort and perceived energy postrace; dropout 9%.

records.title: Cocoa flavanols protect cognitive function, cerebral oxygenation, and mental fatigue during severe hypoxia.

first_pass_scientific_annotation.design_material: Placebo-controlled double-blind trials with 12 participants: cocoa flavanols 15 mg/kg, 90 minutes before cognitive tasks in normoxia and poikilocapnic/isocapnic hypoxia equivalent to 5,500 m. Randomization, preparation constituents and period spacing not stated in abstract.
first_pass_scientific_annotation.measured_function_or_other: Cognitive performance, reaction time, cerebral NIRS oxygenation and subjective mental-fatigue context. No explicit physical task or physical-fatigue measure.
first_pass_scientific_annotation.results_limits: Poikilocapnic overall cognition +4% versus placebo (P = .033), oxygenation signal and fatigue difference, but isocapnic cognition unchanged (1%, P = .72). Reaction time worsened 8% in normoxia and another 11% in isocapnic hypoxia (P = .01). Neuroprotective conclusion must retain condition-specific null/adverse results; physical-function scope unresolved.
